cards.text: Elijah the Tishbite is the man who told Ahab, king of Israel, there'd be no dew or rain except at his word (1 Kings 16:29; 17:1). Now, after a long time, in the third year of the drought, the word of the LORD comes to Elijah again.

cards.question: Three years into the drought, what does the LORD tell Elijah to do?

answers.text: Go and present himself to Ahab
Hide again by the Brook of Cherith
Stay on with the widow in Zarephath

cards.question: The LORD says, "Go and present yourself to Ahab, and I will send ___ upon the face of the earth."

cards.text: So Elijah heads out to face the king. Meanwhile the famine is severe in Samaria, and Ahab summons Obadiah, the man in charge of the palace.

cards.question: Obadiah, the man in charge of Ahab's palace, greatly fears the LORD.

cards.text: When Jezebel, Ahab's wife, slaughtered the prophets of the LORD, Obadiah took a hundred of them and hid them (1 Kings 16:31). A HUNDRED prophets, friend, and I can't hide ONE cookie in my bakery without leaving a crumb trail.

cards.question: How did Obadiah hide those hundred prophets of the LORD?

cards.text: Now Ahab gives Obadiah a job. Go throughout the land, to every spring and every valley.

cards.question: What is Ahab hoping to find at every spring and valley?

answers.text: Grass to keep the horses and mules alive
Grain to feed the hungry people of Samaria
Water to fill up the palace wells again

cards.text: So they divide the land to explore. The KING, friend. Personally. Out in a valley staring at the ground like he dropped a chocolate chip.

cards.question: Once Ahab and Obadiah divide up the land, how do they search it?

answers.text: Each goes his own way by himself
Together with a band of soldiers
Through servants sent from the palace

cards.text: Obadiah's out there on his own, checking springs and valleys. And SUDDENLY, there's Elijah, right in front of him.

cards.question: When Obadiah recognizes Elijah, he falls facedown.

cards.text: Obadiah asks, "Is it you, my lord Elijah?" And "It is I," he answers.

cards.question: What does Elijah tell Obadiah to do next?

answers.text: Go tell Ahab that Elijah is here
Gather the hidden prophets of the LORD
Keep Elijah hidden from King Ahab

cards.text: Friend, I bet Obadiah's stomach just dropped straight into his sandals. This man does NOT like that plan.

cards.question: What does Obadiah think Ahab will do to him if he delivers Elijah's message?

answers.text: Throw him out of the palace
Send him off to search more

cards.text: Obadiah explains: there's no nation or kingdom where Ahab hasn't sent someone to search for Elijah. Friend, I sat in a junk drawer for YEARS and nobody checked one cabinet for me.

cards.question: When a kingdom told Ahab's searchers that Elijah wasn't there, Ahab made that kingdom swear they hadn't found him.

cards.text: And NOW Elijah wants him to walk up to that king and say "Elijah is here!" Obadiah's got another worry, too.

cards.question: What does Obadiah worry will happen to Elijah once Obadiah leaves him?

answers.text: The Spirit of the LORD will carry him off
Ahab's searchers will catch up to him first
He will slip back into hiding by the brook

cards.text: Ahab shows up, finds nobody, and Obadiah's done. Then he reads Elijah his whole résumé: feared the LORD from his youth, hid a hundred prophets, and closes with "He will kill me!"

cards.question: Elijah answers with an oath: "As surely as the LORD of Hosts lives, before whom I stand, I will present myself to Ahab ___."

cards.text: So Obadiah goes and tells Ahab, and Ahab goes to meet Elijah. Every nation, every kingdom, and the big search ends with one guy walking back in going "Uh, boss?"

cards.question: Face to face at last, Ahab says, "Is that you, O ___ of Israel?"

cards.text: Elijah fires right back. "I have not troubled Israel," he says, and he points the finger at Ahab and his father's house.

cards.question: Why does Elijah say Ahab and his father's house have troubled Israel?

answers.text: They forsook the LORD's commandments for the Baals
They kept taxing the people all through the famine
They chased the LORD's prophet out of the land

cards.text: Then the man the king's been hunting everywhere starts giving the KING orders. Summon all Israel, Elijah says.

cards.question: Where does Elijah tell Ahab to summon all Israel to meet him?
Elijah also wants the hundred hidden prophets of the LORD to come to Mount Carmel.

cards.text: He wants the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of Asherah who eat at Jezebel's table, plus ONE Elijah. Pull up a chair, friend, because this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 3 quotes "Go and present yourself to Ahab, and I will send ___ upon the face of the earth.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 12 quotes "As surely as the LORD of Hosts lives, before whom I stand, I will present myself to Ahab ___.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 14 quotes "Is that you, O ___ of Israel?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The story card has three things happening: Elijah heads out to face Ahab, the famine is severe in Samaria, and Ahab summons Obadiah. It should be split.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The setup line "The KING, friend. Personally." says Ahab searches in person. That rules out the wrong answer "Through servants sent from the palace" on card 11 and points toward the right answer "Each goes his own way by himself."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card quotes "It is I," and only then says "he answers," without naming Elijah as the speaker first. The card is also only two bare quotes with no Papa Dorin voice.

rule.text: When he quotes someone speaking as "I," he says who it is first.

findings.problem: "Ahab shows up, finds nobody, and Obadiah's done" states as plain narration what is only Obadiah's conditional fear in 18:12 ("when I go and tell Ahab and he does not find you, he will kill me"). It reads as if it happened, but the text shows that Ahab does find Elijah (18:16-17).

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: Right after "Ahab shows up," the line "Then he reads Elijah his whole résumé... and closes with "He will kill me!"" leaves "he" pointing at Ahab. The first-person quote never names Obadiah as the speaker.

rule.text: When he quotes someone speaking as "I," he says who it is first.

findings.problem: Nothing before this card sets up "troubler." The blank asks the baker to guess Ahab's exact word (troubler vs enemy vs betrayer), not a meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: A baker could argue that the wrong answer "They chased the LORD's prophet out of the land" is right. This passage says Ahab hunted Elijah in every nation and kingdom (18:10), and that Jezebel slaughtered the LORD's prophets (18:4).

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The right answer uses the archaic "forsook," which sounds more like the Bible than the plain modern wrong answers ("kept taxing," "chased").

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The card asks about something that isn't in the passage (the hidden prophets coming to Carmel). Meanwhile the key detail of 18:19, the 450 prophets of Baal and 400 prophets of Asherah, is only told on card 20 and never asked.

rule.text: Ask about the moments that move the passage forward and the details the baker needs to understand it.
